The Rock Texture Atlas is an online reference guide created by the Geological Survey of India (GSI) based on a massive legacy database accumulated over more than 170 years. The portal is divided into 11 thematic chapters and features micrographs taken under an optical microscope, covering igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic rocks, as well as meteorites and gemstones. This resource serves as an open platform for students, researchers, and young specialists, aiding them in mapping, petrographic research, and assessing the economic potential of rocks.

Each page of this site  consists of two parts, descriptive (an exhaustive explanation of the mineral phase) and visual (high-resolution photographs); the information contained on the pages are taken from various university textbooks and scientific papers, cited throughout the text.

description: The presented resource offers an extensive database for studying petrography, including hundreds of high-resolution image pairs of rare rock thin sections and over 1,500 short instructional videos for practicing optical mineralogy outside the lab. Additionally, the continuing education section provides specialized tutorials, digital books, and electron microscopy data designed to deepen the knowledge of advanced undergraduate and graduate students.

description: This site aims to provide information on the characteristics of the minerals under the microscope, both of transparent minerals under the Transmitted Light microscope and of opaque minerals under the Reflected Light microscope, as far as possible and necessary. The site is a translation of the corresponding site in portuguese, using (and revising!) Google Translator. It is in construction; new minerals are added almost every day.
